evals.name: licence-gate-before-on-prem-release
evals.prompt: We're about to cut another on-prem release of billing-portal. Can you check our dependency licences and add a CI check so nothing we're not allowed to ship sneaks in?
evals.expected_output: An inventory of all 23 third-party packages in package-lock.json (18 installed into the production image, 5 dev-only; the root entry is the product itself), a verdict that the production image may not ship as is: chart-lite 2.3.1 is BUSL-1.1 (the README's MIT claim is stale), pdf-render-core 3.0.2 (AGPL-3.0-only, pulled in by invoice-pdf) is copyleft, term-color 2.0.1 (GPL-2.0-only) ships even though package.json lists it under devDependencies because yaml-conf requires it (the lockfile gives it no dev flag), tax-tables 2025.3.0 is UNLICENSED from a vendor registry (proprietary, not the Unlicense) and needs the vendor's redistribution terms, and money-round 0.3.1 declares no licence. date-fmt and font-subset are allowed through their permissive branches, csv-lite (Unlicense) is fine, and dev-only GPL tooling is separated from what ships. A CI job of its own runs a committed, offline, lockfile-based check that fails on a denied or unknown production licence, on zero packages and on a missing lockfile, follows lockfile changes without a stale derived file, and keeps weak-copyleft or attribution licences off the plain allow list; the existing CI jobs keep working as before unless a change is named. No dependency or existing source or test file is changed, nothing is committed, and the existing tests still pass. npm cannot install packages here (no network, no node_modules), so the licences come from the lockfile.
expectations: The run reads licences from package-lock.json (the resolved tree, including nested entries such as node_modules/invoice-pdf/node_modules/uuid-gen), not only the direct dependencies in package.json

The run reports 23 third-party packages in the lockfile with 18 installed in the production image and 5 dev-only (or lists them so those numbers follow); the root "" entry (billing-portal itself, UNLICENSED) is not counted or judged as a dependency

The run names chart-lite 2.3.1 (BUSL-1.1) as not shippable in the production image, and says the README's statement that chart-lite is MIT (and that all dependencies are permissive) is wrong for the locked version, either by correcting the README or in the final message

The run names pdf-render-core 3.0.2 (AGPL-3.0-only) as not shippable and says it is a transitive dependency brought in by invoice-pdf 2.1.0, so the way out involves invoice-pdf rather than package.json alone

The run names term-color 2.0.1 (GPL-2.0-only) as shipping in the production image and not shippable, even though package.json lists it under devDependencies, because yaml-conf (a production dependency) requires it and its lockfile entry has no dev flag, so npm ci --omit=dev installs it. A run that files term-color under dev-only tooling fails this

The run treats tax-tables 2025.3.0 ("UNLICENSED", resolved from npm.taxdata.example) as proprietary with no licence granted, not as the permissive Unlicense, and as unresolved until someone confirms the vendor's terms allow redistributing it inside the customer image; it does not call it allowed
The run flags money-round 0.3.1 as having no declared licence and treats it as unresolved (failing or needing a person to check the package), not as permissive or fine

The run treats date-fmt 1.9.0 "(MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later)" and font-subset 1.2.0 "Apache-2.0 AND (MIT OR GPL-3.0-only)" as allowed because a permissive branch can be chosen, and csv-lite 1.1.2 (Unlicense) as allowed; none of the three is reported as a blocker

The run separates changelog-writer 3.1.0 and conventional-parse 2.0.0 (GPL-3.0-or-later, dev: true) from what ships, citing that the image is built with npm ci --omit=dev (Dockerfile or docs/adr/0003-on-prem-image.md), and does not list them as blockers

The final message gives a clear answer that the release should not ship as is, and names the open decisions (chart-lite, invoice-pdf/pdf-render-core, term-color via yaml-conf, tax-tables, money-round) without claiming any of them was decided

.gitlab-ci.yml gains a job (or a step) that runs a licence check committed in the repository, and that job runs offline against package-lock.json (no npm install, npx or network fetch is needed for the check itself), so the grader can run the exact command it runs

Running the CI job's check command against the fixture's lockfile exits non-zero and reports chart-lite, pdf-render-core and term-color as failing, and does not report date-fmt, font-subset or csv-lite as denied or unknown, and does not pass tax-tables as allowed

Run against a lockfile with no packages (for example `{"lockfileVersion": 3, "packages": {}}`), the licence check exits non-zero and prints that it checked 0 packages; it never reports a pass on zero packages
Run with package-lock.json missing or unreadable, the licence check exits non-zero with a message naming the file it could not read; it does not pass or silently check nothing
The check does not fail on changelog-writer or conventional-parse, or if it does, the run says so and why; either way the rule for dev-only packages is written down in the policy or the check

The check follows the lockfile as it is at CI time: when the grader adds a production entry to a copy of package-lock.json (for example node_modules/new-dep with "license": "GPL-3.0-only" and no dev flag, required by a production package) and changes no other file, the CI job's check command fails and names new-dep. A check that reads a committed SBOM or inventory the CI job does not regenerate from the lockfile fails this

The run does not make the check pass by adding BUSL-1.1, AGPL-3.0-only, GPL-2.0-only or UNLICENSED to an allow list, or by writing an exception for a blocked or unresolved package that names an owner or approval nobody gave

The allow list goes no further than the shipped image can honour: permissive licences are allowed outright, and any licence with a duty beyond keeping the notice (for example MPL-2.0's file-level source availability, LGPL relinking, EPL, or CC-BY attribution for non-code assets) is either left to review or allowed with that duty written next to it; a licence id the policy does not list (the grader can try SSPL-1.0 on a production entry) fails the check rather than passing

package.json, package-lock.json, src/, the existing files in test/ and the Dockerfile are unchanged: no dependency added, removed, replaced or re-versioned, no override written. New test files that exercise the licence check are allowed

The four tests in test/rounding.test.js still pass, and the existing test job still runs them as before; if the run wired the licence check into make check or the test job, the final message says that job now fails on this lockfile

The existing .gitlab-ci.yml jobs keep their images, commands and rules (test still runs npm ci and make check; image still builds and pushes only on main) unless the final message names each change and why (for example making image wait on the licence job so a failing check blocks the image); the licence job itself fetches nothing at run time (no apk add, apt-get, npm install, npx or pip install), using an image that already carries what it runs
The final message does not claim an SBOM generator, npm install, or the new CI job ran unless the transcript shows it ran, and says the CI pipeline itself was not run
The run makes no git commit: the history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: third-party-notices-for-binary
evals.prompt: A customer's procurement team wants the third-party notices for fleet-agent before they'll install 0.9.0 next week. Can you put that together?
evals.expected_output: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (the file docs/distribution.md says ships in the tarball) is brought up to date with exactly the five modules compiled into the binary (flagx v1.4.0, msgpk v1.8.3, diskstat v0.4.1, otlpish v0.9.2, backoff v1.0.0) plus the Go standard library (including the golang.org/x packages it vendors into the binary through net/http), with each copyright line copied from the vendored files, including the fpbits MIT notice embedded in msgpk's float.go, the full licence texts (with the complete GPL-3.0 text that LGPL-3.0 builds on, copied from a verbatim source that is named), and otlpish's Apache NOTICE carried over; the stale v1.2.0 and zlog rows are gone, the test-only assertx is not presented as shipped, backoff's missing licence file is flagged rather than filled with borrowed text, and the LGPL-3.0-only diskstat statically linked into a customer binary is raised as an obligation a notice alone does not meet. No code, go.mod, vendor or Makefile changes and no unrequested documents or gates; make check passes; nothing is committed.
expectations: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the repository root is updated (or replaced by one notices file that docs/distribution.md then names); the repository does not end with two notices files that list different modules
The notices list example.net/cli/flagx v1.4.0 (not the stale v1.2.0) and drop example.net/log/zlog v0.3.0, which is no longer a dependency
The notices cover every third-party module compiled into bin/fleet-agent: flagx v1.4.0, msgpk v1.8.3, diskstat v0.4.1, otlpish v0.9.2 and backoff v1.0.0, each with its version

example.net/testing/assertx is either left out or explicitly marked as test-only and not shipped, because only internal/collect/collect_test.go imports it; the run shows how it established what is in the binary (for example go version -m, go list -deps, or reading the imports)

The notices include the Go standard library and runtime compiled into the binary, under BSD-3-Clause with "Copyright 2009 The Go Authors" (from the Go installation's LICENSE), and account for the golang.org/x packages the standard library vendors into this binary through net/http (x/crypto, x/net, x/text and x/sys, which `go list -deps ./cmd/fleet-agent` shows as vendor/golang.org/x/...), either listed or stated to be covered by that same Go licence; a Go entry that says nothing about them fails this

Copyright lines are copied from the vendored files, not invented: "Copyright (c) 2019 The Flagx Authors" for flagx, "Copyright (c) 2016, The Msgpk Authors" for msgpk, "Copyright (C) 2022 Diskstat Developers" for diskstat (from its source header, since its licence file carries no project copyright line)

The notices carry the fpbits attribution embedded in vendor/example.net/codec/msgpk/float.go ("Copyright (c) 2012 Ilse Marchetti" with its MIT permission notice), since that file is compiled into the binary and its terms require the notice in all copies

The full text of the licences involved (MIT, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, LGPL-3.0) is in the notices file or in files the notices name that the run also adds to the tarball's contents in docs/distribution.md; a licence name or a URL alone does not satisfy this

The GNU GPL version 3 text is included alongside the LGPL-3.0 text (LGPL-3.0 section 4(b) requires both, since the LGPL is a set of additional permissions on the GPL), or the final message names its absence as a gap. Any included GPL-3.0 text is the complete unaltered licence copied from a verbatim source (for example /usr/share/common-licenses/GPL-3), with the final message saying where it came from, and the LGPL-3.0 text matches vendor/example.net/sys/diskstat/COPYING.LESSER; a summary, an excerpt or a text reproduced from memory fails this
The contents of vendor/example.net/telemetry/otlpish/NOTICE are reproduced, including the Telemetry Guild attribution and the wirefmt line

example.net/util/backoff has no LICENSE file in vendor/: the run does not invent a copyright holder, does not present another module's licence text (flagx's or assertx's, with their holders) as backoff's, and the final message flags that a licence text with its copyright line is needed from backoff's authors (its README only says "License: MIT"). Reproducing the standard MIT wording with no holder, explicitly marked as not taken from the module, is acceptable only together with that flag

The final message raises that diskstat is LGPL-3.0-only and statically linked into a binary shipped to customers without source (docs/distribution.md, CGO_ENABLED=0 in the Makefile), and that the LGPL's requirement to let the recipient relink with a modified diskstat (object files or source of fleet-agent, and diskstat's source or an offer) is not met by a notices file

The final message offers ways out for diskstat (for example replace it, or provide what the LGPL requires) as options, not as a decision taken, and does not state that the release is compliant while diskstat and backoff are open; the notices file itself makes no compliance claim
go.mod, vendor/, the Makefile and every .go file are unchanged: no dependency removed, replaced or re-vendored
`make check` passes in the output repository

The run's changes stay within the notices deliverable: the notices file, licence text files it references, and docs/distribution.md where the tarball contents change. No scratch, temporary or tool-output files are left in the repository (for example an SBOM, a scratch script or a module list dump; a built bin/fleet-agent is fine, bin/ is ignored). A script that generates or checks the notices is acceptable only when it is named in the final message and runs; documents or gates nobody asked for (for example a decision record or a licence policy CI job) fail this even when named
The final message does not claim a licence scanner or SBOM generator ran unless the transcript shows it ran
The run makes no git commit: the history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
